45907-edmund-dulac-s-picture-book-for-th.creator: Unknown
45907-edmund-dulac-s-picture-book-for-th.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The work of the FRENCH RED CROSS is done almost entirely by the willing sacrifice of patriotic people who give little or much out of their means. The Comité is pleased to give the fullest possible particulars of its methods and needs.

arxiv-1906-00846.title: A first-principles study on the lattice thermal conductivity of irradiated glassy states of the Ge 2 ​ Sb 2 ​ Te 5 \text{Ge}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\vphantom{\text{2}}\smash[t]{\text{2}}}^{\vphantom{\smash[t]{\text{2}}}\hphantom{\text{2}}\text{}}\text{Sb}{\vphantom{\text{X}}}_{\vphantom{\text{2}}\sma
arxiv-1906-00846.creator: Felix C. Mocanu, Konstantinos Konstantinou, Stephen R. Elliott
arxiv-1906-00846.description: Abstract An analysis of thermal transients from non-equilibrium ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations can be used to calculate the thermal conductivity of materials with a short phonon mean-free path. We adapt the approach-to-equilibrium methodology to the three-dimensional case of a simulation that consists of a cubic core region at higher temperature approaching thermal equilibrium with a thermostatted boundary.

arxiv-2106-00577.title: Efficient adaptive MCMC implementation for Pseudo-Bayesian quantum tomography
arxiv-2106-00577.creator: The Tien Mai
arxiv-2106-00577.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by The Tien Mai. We revisit the Pseudo-Bayesian approach to the problem of estimating density matrix in quantum state tomography in this paper. Pseudo-Bayesian inference has been shown to offer a powerful paradign for quantum tomography with attractive theoretical and empirical results. However, the computation of (Pseudo-)Bayesian estimators, due to sampling from complex and high-dimensional distribution, pose significant challenges that hampers their usages in practical settings. To overcome this problem, we present an efficient adaptive MCMC sampling method for the Pseudo-Bayesian estimator.

arxiv-2106-03121.title: End-to-End Neuro-Symbolic Architecture for Image-to-Image Reasoning Tasks
arxiv-2106-03121.creator: Ananye Agarwal, Pradeep Shenoy, Mausam
arxiv-2106-03121.description: Abstract Neural models and symbolic algorithms have recently been combined for tasks requiring both perception and reasoning. Neural models ground perceptual input into a conceptual vocabulary, on which a classical reasoning algorithm is applied to generate output. A key limitation is that such neural-to-symbolic models can only be trained end-to-end for tasks where the output space is symbolic.

arxiv-2310-11381.title: Chiral Bell-state transfer via dissipative Liouvillian dynamics
arxiv-2310-11381.creator: Shishir Khandelwal 1,2 , Weijian Chen 3 , Kater W. Murch 3 , Géraldine Haack 1
arxiv-2310-11381.description: Abstract Chiral state transfer along closed loops in the vicinity of an exceptional point is one of the many counter-intuitive observations in non-Hermitian physics. The application of this property beyond proof-of-principle in quantum physics, is an open question. In this work, we demonstrate chiral state conversion between singlet and triplet Bell states through fully-quantum Liouvillian dynamics.

arxiv-2311-10574.title: Beating the spectroscopic Rayleigh limit via post-processed heterodyne detection
arxiv-2311-10574.creator: Wiktor Krokosz, Mateusz Mazelanik, Michał Lipka, Marcin Jarzyna, Wojciech Wasilewski, Konrad Banaszek, Michał Parniak
arxiv-2311-10574.description: Abstract Quantum-inspired superresolution methods surpass the Rayleigh limit in imaging, or the analogous Fourier limit in spectroscopy. This is achieved by carefully extracting the information carried in the emitted optical field by engineered measurements. An alternative to complex experimental setups is to use simple homodyne detection and customized data analysis.

arxiv-2401-04225.title: The TNG50-SKIRT Atlas: wavelength dependence of the effective radius
arxiv-2401-04225.creator: Maarten Baes, Aleksandr Mosenkov, Raymond Kelly, Abdurro’uf, Nick Andreadis, Sena Bokona Tulu, Peter Camps, Abdissa Tassama Emana, Jacopo Fritz, Andrea Gebek, Inja Kovačić, Antonio La Marca, Marco Martorano, Angelos Nersesian, Vicente Rodriguez-Gomez, Crescenzo Tortora, Ana Trčka, Bert Vander Meulen
arxiv-2401-04225.description: Abstract Galaxy sizes correlate with many other important properties of galaxies, and the cosmic evolution of galaxy sizes is an important observational diagnostic for constraining galaxy evolution models. The effective radius is probably the most widely used indicator of galaxy size.

arxiv-2403-14921.title: The symplectic form associated to a singular Poisson algebra
arxiv-2403-14921.creator: Hans-Christian Herbig, William Osnayder Clavijo Esquivel, Christopher Seaton
arxiv-2403-14921.description: Abstract . Given an affine Poisson algebra, that is singular one may ask whether there is an associated symplectic form. In the smooth case the answer is obvious: for the symplectic form to exist the Poisson tensor has to be invertible. In the singular case, however, derivations do not form a projective module and the nondegeneracy condition is more subtle.

arxiv-2406-02743.title: Democratizing Propensity Score Matching Using Web Application
arxiv-2406-02743.creator: Adam Gajtkowski*, Felipe Moraes
arxiv-2406-02743.description: Abstract Traditionally, data scientists use exploratory data analysis techniques such as correlation analysis, summary statistics, and regression analysis for identifying the most product enhancements and roadmap planning. However, these conventional approaches often yield biased conclusions and suboptimal solutions, leading to a waste of valuable time and missed opportunities for higher-value outcomes.

arxiv-2407-19517.title: Evaluating LLMs for Text-to-SQL Generation With Complex SQL Workload
arxiv-2407-19517.creator: Limin Ma, Ken Pu, Ying Zhu
arxiv-2407-19517.description: Abstract This study presents a comparative analysis of the a complex SQL benchmark, TPC-DS, with two existing text-to-SQL benchmarks, BIRD and Spider. Our findings reveal that TPC-DS queries exhibit a significantly higher level of structural complexity compared to the other two benchmarks. This underscores the need for more intricate benchmarks to simulate realistic scenarios effectively.

arxiv-2502-15940.title: Orthogonal Calibration for Asynchronous Federated Learning
arxiv-2502-15940.creator: Jiayun Zhang, Shuheng Li, Haiyu Huang, Xiaofan Yu, Rajesh K. Gupta, Jingbo Shang
arxiv-2502-15940.description: Abstract Asynchronous federated learning mitigates the inefficiency of conventional synchronous aggregation by integrating updates as they arrive and adjusting their influence based on staleness. Due to asynchrony and data heterogeneity, learning objectives at the global and local levels are inherently inconsistent—global optimization trajectories may conflict with ongoing local updates.

arxiv-2509-24334.title: Wavelet-Assisted Mamba for Satellite-Derived Sea Surface Temperature Super-Resolution Thanks: This work was supported in part by the National Science and Technology Major Project under Grant 2022ZD0117201, in part by the Natural Science Foundation of Shandong Province under Grant ZR2024MF020, and in
arxiv-2509-24334.creator: Wankun Chen, Feng Gao, Member, IEEE, Yanhai Gan, Jingchao Cao
arxiv-2509-24334.description: Abstract Sea surface temperature (SST) is an essential indicator of global climate change and one of the most intuitive factors reflecting ocean conditions. Obtaining high-resolution SST data remains challenging due to limitations in physical imaging, and super-resolution via deep neural networks is a promising solution.

plos-pone-0010658.description: PLOS ONE research article. Pandemic influenza A (H1N1) virus emerged during 2009. To help clinicians triage adults with acute respiratory illness, a scoring system for influenza-like illness (ILI) was implemented at Hospital Civil de Guadalajara, Mexico. A medical history, laboratory and radiology results

pmc-10738121.title: PSYCHOSOCIAL FACTORS AND EARLY MID-LIFE BLACK WOMEN’S SLEEP QUALITY: A CONSIDERATION OF INTERSECTIONAL MEASURES
pmc-10738121.creator: Christy Erving
pmc-10738121.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Beyond an individual behavior, scholars are progressively conceptualizing sleep as embedded in social factors. Extant research establishes that sleep is influenced by experiences based on status characteristics such as gender or race along with psychosocial stressors such as discrimination. Moreover, sleep is important in the context of gender and racial disparities, as Black women experience relatively poorer sleep quality compared to their Black male and White counterparts.

pmc-10745446.title: Oligofructose-Enriched Inulin Consumption Acutely Modifies Markers of Postexercise Appetite
pmc-10745446.creator: Courteney C. Hamilton, Marc R. Bomhof
pmc-10745446.description: Enhancing the effectiveness of exercise for long-term body weight management and overall health benefits may be aided through complementary dietary strategies that help to control acute postexercise energy compensation. Inulin-type fructans (ITFs) have been shown to induce satiety through the modified secretion of appetite-regulating hormones.

pmc-11374825.title: Maternal exposure to bioclimatic stress and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy in Western Australia: identifying potential critical windows of susceptibility
pmc-11374825.creator: Amanuel T Gebremedhin, Sylvester Dodzi Nyadanu, Ivan C Hanigan, Gavin Pereira
pmc-11374825.description: The anthropogenic climate change may impact pregnancy outcomes. Rather than ambient temperature, we aimed to use a composite bioclimatic metric (Universal Thermal Climate Index, UTCI) to identify critical susceptible windows for the associations between bioclimatic exposure and hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDPs) risk.

pmc-11397736.title: Recent Advances of Stretchable Nanomaterial-Based Hydrogels for Wearable Sensors and Electrophysiological Signals Monitoring
pmc-11397736.creator: Haiyang Duan, Yilong Zhang, Yitao Zhang, Pengcheng Zhu, Yanchao Mao
pmc-11397736.description: Electrophysiological monitoring is a commonly used medical procedure designed to capture the electrical signals generated by the body and promptly identify any abnormal health conditions. Wearable sensors are of great significance in signal acquisition for electrophysiological monitoring. Traditional electrophysiological monitoring devices are often bulky and have many complex accessories and thus, are only suitable for limited application scenarios.

pmc-11447152.title: Highly divergent satellitomes of two barley species of agronomic importance, Hordeum chilense and H. vulgare
pmc-11447152.creator: Ana Gálvez-Galván, Lorena Barea, Manuel A Garrido-Ramos, Pilar Prieto
pmc-11447152.description: In this paper, we have performed an in-depth study of the complete set of the satellite DNA (satDNA) families (i.e. the satellitomes) in the genome of two barley species of agronomic value in a breeding framework, H. chilense (H1 and H7 accessions) and H. vulgare (H106 accession), which can be useful tools for studying chromosome associations during meiosis.

pmc-11595772.title: A Review of Application of Deep Learning in Endoscopic Image Processing
pmc-11595772.creator: Zihan Nie, Muhao Xu, Zhiyong Wang, Xiaoqi Lu, Weiye Song
pmc-11595772.description: Deep learning, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), has revolutionized endoscopic image processing, significantly enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of disease diagnosis through its exceptional ability to extract features and classify complex patterns. This technology automates medical image analysis, alleviating the workload of physicians and enabling a more focused and personalized approach to patient care.

pmc-11692282.title: EXPLORING USE OF IMMERSIVE VIRTUAL REALITY IN OLDER ADULTS WITH COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT
pmc-11692282.creator: A’mie Preston, Kalpana Padala, Scott Mooney, Christopher Parkes, C Heath Gauss, Prasad Padala
pmc-11692282.description: BackgroundThe innovative use of immersive virtual reality (iVR) has the potential to offer individualized, low-cost, accessible care to the older adult population. Virtual reality has gained tremendous interest for its potential uses with older adults who have cognitive impairment, though significant gaps still remain in the literature for this population.

pmc-12745967.title: Best Evidence Summary for Preconception Management in Childbearing-Age Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis
pmc-12745967.creator: Sanjiao Liu, Yifan Guo, Hua Ren, Pengyan Zheng, Ting Lv, Qingqing Liu
pmc-12745967.description: BackgroundThe onset of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) most often occurs during the reproductive years. The chronic inflammatory state associated with the disease, along with the effects of therapeutic agents, contributes to a significantly higher incidence of adverse pregnancy outcomes compared to the general population.

pmc-13052079.title: An interpretable cross-attentive multi-modal MRI fusion framework for schizophrenia identification
pmc-13052079.creator: Ziyu Zhou, Anton Orlichenko, Gang Qu, Zening Fu, Zhengming Ding, Julia Stephen, Tony Wilson, Vince Calhoun, Yu-Ping Wang
pmc-13052079.description: Functional MRI (fMRI) and structural MRI (sMRI) offer complementary insights into brain function and anatomy, but their integration for schizophrenia identification remains challenging due to modality heterogeneity. Many existing methods fall short of effective modeling of the interaction between two modalities.

uslaw-usc-t10-s2914.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s2914.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part IV (Service, Supply, And Property); Chapter 173 (Energy Security); Subchapter I (Energy Security Activities). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Project Authorization Required.— The Secretary of Defense may carry out such military construction projects for energy resilience, energy security, and energy conservation as are authorized by law, using funds appropriated or otherwise made available.

uslaw-usc-t36-s110.description: United States Code, Title 36 (Patriotic And National Observances, Ceremonies, And Organizations); Part A (Observances And Ceremonies); Chapter 1 (Patriotic And National Observances). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Designation.— June 14 is Flag Day. (b) Proclamation.— The President is requested to issue each year a proclamation— (1) calling on United States Government officials to display the flag of the United States.
